The himg/hact helpers already factor the repeated hdX/hdY/hsX/... steps. I found one clear repeated argument that deserves a shared lemma: the odd-prime "c⁻¹ = c and c^p = 1 imply c = 1" reasoning, which is written out twice. The other repetitions are short (hcen/hc definitions, the fin_cases conj lemmas) or are thin wrappers, so I did not report them. Both hfix hypotheses should have the form c⁻¹ = c after the rewrites, from my reading of the rw/nth_rewrite chains. That orientation is the main uncertainty.

findings.problem: The same argument is written out twice. A commutator c is fixed by an automorphism that sends it to its inverse, so c⁻¹ = c. Together with c ^ p = 1 and p odd, this gives c = 1. First c ^ 2 = 1 is derived from c⁻¹ = c. Then p = 2k+1 is split off, and pow_succ, pow_mul, hc2, one_pow, one_mul are applied to c ^ p = 1. The block in commute_of_fix_of_inv (lines 162–171) is repeated almost verbatim for the c02 case at lines 298–308, down to the hpodd/omega bookkeeping. Only the choice of commutator (⁅g,h⁆ versus ⁅g 0, g 2⁆) differs. Any change to the oddness argument has to be made in both places, and the c02 block makes the main splitting proof longer.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a lemma in the Splitting section before commute_of_fix_of_inv:

theorem eq_one_of_inv_eq_of_pow_prime (hp2 : p ≠ 2) {c : P} (hcp : c ^ p = 1) (hfix : c⁻¹ = c) : c = 1

Proof sketch: hpodd from hp.out.odd_of_ne_two hp2. Get c ^ 2 = 1 via `rw [sq]; nth_rewrite 1 [← hfix]; exact inv_mul_cancel c`. Then write p = 2*k+1 and rewrite hcp with pow_succ, pow_mul, hc2, one_pow, one_mul.

Use 1, in commute_of_fix_of_inv, after `rw [hinv] at hfix` and `set c := ⁅g, h⁆`, replace lines 162–171 by `exact commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm.1 (eq_one_of_inv_eq_of_pow_prime hp2 (hcp g h) hfix)`.

Use 2, in c02, after `set c := ⁅g 0, g 2⁆`, delete hpodd, hc2 and hc1 (lines 298–307) and close with `exact commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm.1 (eq_one_of_inv_eq_of_pow_prime hp2 (hcp (g 0) (g 2)) hfix)`.

Both uses sit inside `variable {P} [Group P] {p} [hp : Fact p.Prime]`, so no new imports or hypotheses are needed. In both places hfix should already have the form c⁻¹ = c after the existing rewrites. I have not compiled this.
findings.benefit: The odd-order cancellation is stated and proved once under a name that says what it does. commute_of_fix_of_inv ends in a single line, and the c02 branch of the 150-line splitting theorem shrinks by about ten lines. Readers can see that both commutator arguments rest on the same fact. Any later fix to the oddness reasoning is made in one place.
